title: Hom complex comparison with its specified product projections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $U$ an open [def-pc-scheme]. Write $L$ for the equivalence from module sheaves on the over-$U$ site to module sheaves on $U$, and $T$ for its degreewise functor on integer cochain complexes. Let $P$ be a complex on the over-site. Given isomorphisms $e(A,B):L\mathcal{H}om(A,B)\cong\mathcal{H}om(LA,LB)$ natural for precomposition in $A$ and postcomposition in $B$, there are isomorphisms $b(M):T\mathcal{H}om^\bullet(P,M)\cong\mathcal{H}om^\bullet(TP,TM)$ [def-pur-hom-complex], natural in every chain map $M\to N$. For the specified product projections [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections], $b(M)^n;\pi_{TP,TM,n,r,s}=L(\pi_{P,M,n,r,s});e(P^r,M^s)$ for every $r+n=s$. The source projection is [def-pc-ordinary-evaluation-data]. No boundedness or homological hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Preserve the specified product fan under the equivalence. The forward map to the target product is the lift of the mapped source projections followed by e; the inverse uses the inverse e. Product extensionality and cancellation prove that the two maps are inverse.

Postcompose the chain-map equation with each target product projection. Substitute the differential formulas. Apply naturality of e to each composition term and additivity of L to the difference and its integer sign. Assemble the degree isomorphisms with HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents.

For naturality in M, postcompose in each degree with each target product projection, substitute the Hom bifunctor map formula, and use the given naturality of e. Joint monicity of product projections proves the equality. The same construction retains the projection equation.

theorem exists_homComplex_overEquiv_projections (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (P : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ) :
    let L := Equivalence.functor
      (C := localEvaluationModules X U)
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)
    let T := L.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    ∀ (e : ∀ A B : localEvaluationModules X U,
        L.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf.over U) A B) ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) (L.obj A) (L.obj B)),
      (∀ (A A' B B' : localEvaluationModules X U) (f : A' ⟶ A) (g : B ⟶ B'),
        L.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf.over U) f g) ≫
            (e A' B').hom =
          (e A B).hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.toScheme.sheaf)
            (L.map f) (L.map g)) →
      ∃ b : ∀ M : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ,
          T.obj (homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P M) ≅
            homComplex (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) (T.obj P) (T.obj M),
        (∀ (M N : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ) (a : M ⟶ N),
          T.map (((homComplexFunctor (R := X.sheaf.over U)).obj (op P)).map a) ≫
              (b N).hom =
            (b M).hom ≫ ((homComplexFunctor (R := U.toScheme.sheaf)).obj
              (op (T.obj P))).map (T.map a)) ∧
        (∀ (M : CochainComplex (localEvaluationModules X U) ℤ)
            (n r s : ℤ) (h : r + n = s),
          (b M).hom.f n ≫
              (Classical.choose (homComplex_projections_exists.{u, u, u, u}
                (R := U.toScheme.sheaf)))
                (T.obj P) (T.obj M) n r s h =
            L.map (localEvaluationProjection X U P M n r s h) ≫
              (e (P.X r) (M.X s)).hom)
